welcome_lead: You'll meet ethical business behaviour and the idea of corporate social responsibility.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acting ethically means doing what is morally right — even when it isn't legally required.

It covers honesty in advertising, paying suppliers on time, and treating staff fairly.

CSR is the wider duty to society and the planet.

Examples: paying living wages, sourcing fair-trade ingredients, reducing emissions, supporting communities.

Ethical choices often raise costs: pricier suppliers, slower expansion, more reporting.

But they can boost brand image, customer loyalty and staff motivation — paying back over time.

options: Paying suppliers late
Sourcing from a fair-trade farm

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder?
options: A shareholder owns shares in the company; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or with interest in the business — employees, customers, suppliers, community, plus shareholders.
Stakeholders are managers and shareholders are workers.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Stakeholders and shareholders are different spellings of the same word.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
